name: Peptide eye creams (Eyeliss, Haloxyl)

card.summary: Eye creams built on branded cosmetic peptide complexes marketed for bags and dark circles; claims come mainly from ingredient marketing.
card.aka: Eyeliss, Haloxyl, palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 eye creams
card.note: Published independent trials of these named complexes were not found in the sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
Eyeliss and Haloxyl are trade names of cosmetic ingredient blends containing short peptides, sold to makers of under-eye creams with claims about reducing puffiness (bags) and dark circles.

The sources available for this entry do not include trial data on these specific blends, so the claims are best understood as manufacturer and marketing positions rather than established results.
quick.mechanism: Cosmetic peptides are short amino-acid chains. Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, a peptide used in skin creams, is described as derived from an immunoglobulin G sequence and claimed to reduce interleukin-6 and support collagen. Whether such peptides cross the skin in meaningful amounts is discussed in reviews of cosmetic peptides.
quick.risks: Cosmetic-grade peptide creams are sold without prescription. No specific safety data on these blends were found in the sources reviewed; general eyelid-skin irritation from cosmetic ingredients can occur.

lead: Eyeliss and Haloxyl are trade names of peptide-containing cosmetic ingredient complexes used in under-eye creams and marketed for puffiness and dark circles. They are ingredients supplied to cosmetic formulators rather than medicines, and people use eye creams containing them in the hope of a smoother, less shadowed, less puffy under-eye area that looks more rested.

Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, one cosmetic peptide of this kind, is described as a synthetic peptide derived from a sequence in immunoglobulin G, with a fatty-acid (palmitoyl) chain attached so it dissolves better in skin lipids and penetrates more easily. It is claimed to give anti-wrinkle effects, to promote collagen synthesis and to reduce interleukin-6 production.[1] Its reference literature consists largely of reviews of cosmetic peptides and skin permeability rather than trial results for the peptide alone.[1]

Dark circles have several causes, including heredity, thin lower-eyelid skin, pigmentation, blood vessels showing through, allergies, fatigue and ageing, so a single peptide-based product may address some presentations and not others.[2]

chain: Peptide complex applied under the eyes
Claimed support for skin firmness and calmer inflammation
Smoother, less puffy, less dark under-eye look
angle.text: Peptide eye creams are applied around the eyes to make the skin look firmer and less puffy or shadowed. They are used as a daily skincare step, often alongside moisturisers and ingredients such as caffeine or vitamin C.

paras: These products are sold in the eye-care category, where peptides are combined with moisturisers and other actives such as caffeine or vitamin C. General references on dark circles describe caffeine as a vasoconstrictor said to tighten dilated vessels, and vitamin C as brightening pigmentation and thickening the dermis; peptides are not discussed there.[2]

Palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 is grouped with matrikine peptides, which are reported to promote collagen synthesis, although it is not derived from connective tissue proteins, and it is reported to dampen inflammatory signalling through interleukin-6.[1] Mechanisms specific to the branded Eyeliss and Haloxyl blends were not described in the references reviewed.

Reference works list heredity, bruising, anatomy such as thin lower-eyelid skin, allergies and eye rubbing, sun exposure, nutritional deficiencies, fatigue and age-related collagen and fat loss among the causes of dark circles.[2] Treatments described include topical creams, laser and intense pulsed light, hyaluronic acid fillers and fat transfer.[2]

No studies found. A 2023 clinical study of a multi-peptide anti-aging eye serum is listed in the reference list of the palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 article, but it does not test Eyeliss or Haloxyl specifically.[1]
